narration.full_text: Control and coordination in our bodies are primarily handled by the nervous and muscular tissues. The nervous tissue is a specialized network of nerve cells, also known as neurons, designed to conduct information through electrical impulses from one part of the body to another. The nervous system itself is this entire network of conducting tissues that receives stimuli and transmits them throughout the body. The fundamental units that make up this intricate system are called nerve cells or neurons. Receptors gather information and pass it to the brain via a specific type of nerve cells called sensory neurons. Conversely, motor neurons are responsible for transmitting information from the brain to the effector organs, which are mainly muscles and glands. A nerve impulse is essentially information in the form of chemical and electrical signals that travel through neurons. These impulses are initially carried by dendrites towards the cell body. The neuromuscular junction is a critical point where a muscle fiber makes contact with a motor neuron. This motor neuron carries nerve impulses from the central nervous system. The impulses move from the neuron to the muscle fibers using neurotransmitters, much like how impulses are transmitted across a synapse between two neurons. Voluntary actions are those that require conscious thought and are performed knowingly. Examples include speaking to a friend or writing a letter. In contrast, involuntary actions are not under an individual's conscious control. They are automatic responses to stimuli and are not governed by the voluntary control of the brain. An example of this is unknowingly touching a hot plate. Reflex action is a quick, sudden, and immediate response of the body to a stimulus. Think of a knee jerk or withdrawing your hand instantly after touching a hot object. The pathway through which a nerve impulse travels during a reflex action is known as a reflex arc.

visual_beats.description: Text: Control and coordination are provided by nervous and muscular tissues.
Text: Nervous tissue: made up of an organized network of nerve cells or neurons, specialized for conduction information via electrical impulses.
Text: Nervous system: system of conducting tissues that receives the stimulus and transmits it to other parts of the body forming a network of nerves.
Term: Nerve cells or neurons. Definition: The units which make up the nervous system.
Term: Sensory neurons. Definition: Nerve cells that pass information from receptors to the brain.
Text: Motor neurons transmit information from the brain to effector organs (muscles and glands).
Term: Nerve Impulse. Definition: Information in the form of chemical and electrical signals passing through neurons, carried by dendrites towards the cell body.

Term: Neuromuscular Junction. Definition: The point where a muscle fibre contacts a motor neuron carrying nerve impulses from the central nervous system. Impulses travel from neuron to muscle fibres via neurotransmitters.
Term: Voluntary Action. Definition: Actions that need thinking and are performed knowingly, controlled by conscious thought. Example: Speaking, writing.
Term: Involuntary Action. Definition: Automatic responses to a stimulus, not under the control of individual will or voluntary brain control. Example: Touching a hot plate unknowingly.
Text: Reflex action: quick, sudden and immediate response of the body to a stimulus. E.g., Knee jerk, withdrawal of hand on touching hot object.
Text: Reflex arc: The pathway through which nerve impulse pass during reflex action.
